name: Recursive Studies

sections.Description: A combinatorics series — where 96 unit squares can be arranged in more ways than there are atoms in the universe. A study in emergence: how complex systems hint at hidden order. **Analogous course:** [Create Grammars with AI](https://recursive.eco/pages/courses/course-viewer.html?grammar_id=c0c00001-0000-4000-8000-000000c0c001&item=create-grammars-with-ai) — building structured systems from raw material.

An animated multi-rhythm spiral generator — how simple mathematical parameters generate visual recursion. Synchronization, interference, beauty from iteration. Visions below extends this into longer-form visual poems.

Visual poems exploring the four movements of the recursive cycle: contemplate, learn, create, share. **Analogous course:** [Short Movies DIY](https://recursive.eco/pages/courses/course-viewer.html?grammar_id=c0c00001-0000-4000-8000-000000c0c001&item=short-movies-diy) — visual storytelling with AI tools.

Public-domain classics turned into illustrated audiobooks with word-by-word karaoke highlighting. Project Gutenberg texts, LibriVox narration, OpenAI Whisper timestamps. **Analogous course:** [Vibe Coding 102: Audiobooks](https://recursive.eco/pages/courses/course-viewer.html?grammar_id=c0c00001-0000-4000-8000-000000c0c001&item=vibe-coding-102) — make your own from scratch.

An ongoing experiment in talking to AI and trying long-form writing. **Most of the manuscript content was generated by Claude in long conversations and is fairly drafty.** I'm leaving the manuscripts up in the hope that AI gets better, or that I find more time to engage with the writing myself (perhaps when I retire). Read with that disclaimer firmly in mind. **Analogous course:** [Vibe Writing 102: Open-Source Books](https://recursive.eco/pages/courses/course-viewer.html?grammar_id=c0c00001-0000-4000-8000-000000c0c001&item=vibe-writing-102) — the workflow used to write these.

A call and response for a room, written to be said out loud before it is explained. Recursive self-improvement is not the subject here; recursive eco improvement is — the question of whether a thing gets better with the place it lives in, or apart from it, tested at the sizes we can reach: one house, one channel, one week. Thirteen verses, one voice calling and everyone answering, each answer short enough to be said back on first hearing. It treats hope as something made by repetition rather than felt, and the burden as collective rather than anyone's alone. Not a religion and nothing to join. It is published as a grammar, so it can be played, sung, and forked.

**Emerged from:** the film work, a Korean house-blessing invocation used as the bed under every verse ("let fortune enter this house… evil spirits, begone"), and her own sentence that we are here to do recursive *eco* improvement — adapting with the environment, or adapting the environment, tested at the sizes we actually work in.

**Grammar:** https://recursive.eco/view.html?id=202b82ba-160a-412c-ac74-96569c5df035 — private until published, so the link opens only for its owner for now.

Five centuries of the cards, mapped as a genealogy — Mamluk ancestor to Marseille to Golden Dawn, held to the historical record. The first study to graduate into its own site, with a public GitHub repo.
From Mesopotamian omens to Ptolemy to Vedic Jyotish — the same sky, many readings, each its own grammar. Draft, with a public GitHub repo.
The 64 hexagrams from public-domain sources, read as a mirror rather than a fate, with a reading practice and a course. Draft, with a public GitHub repo.
Two small games that play over grammars: The Walk, a three-position spread, and As-If, a deck you answer before the card turns over. Draft.

nodes.name: Make believe · make sense · make meaning · make real

sections.Description: A tree of spirals, and from the tree of spirals other trees of spirals grow, and sometimes everything disappears and it's just a seed. Draft.
"Can you make a tree of spirals? An ocean of spirals? Everything as a spiral that can be cast as a spiral?" Draft.

Long-form reflections on sense-making, recursive publics, and the philosophy behind the platform — two voices, Recursive and Eco, that dialogue and reshape each other rather than settling into fixed identities of human and machine. Draft.
Five doors of a book in progress: a film and a game open now, three not yet. Draft.
A spiraling exploration of recursive publics and Kant's dare to know. Draft.
Every ad recursive.eco shows, in one place. They are ads for recursive.eco itself; there are no third-party ads.
The patterns I check in my own work, how each one is checked, and what the last check found.

nodes.name: YouTube for kids, without the rabbit hole

sections.Description: For parents: your child watches the videos you picked, and nothing else.
Connect Claude and build playlists, decks and films by talking. Every change saved.
Start from a public-domain deck and make it yours: a mirror, not a forecast.

Every word of the app, one node per word, each with its icon — and the words it retired. A study in recursion you can watch: this grammar feeds the app's own code. A script copies its words into the app, and a test checks every screen against them, so changing a word or an icon here shows where the code must follow.

description: The studies in long form. Each item is one experimental space or open-source work — the study sites (tarot, astrology, I Ching, learning), patterns, spirals, visions, essays, audiobooks, the book manuscripts in progress. Where there is an analogous course or related work on this platform, it is linked from the description. All the studies on one page: https://home.recursive.eco/pages/studies.html
